pr_body:
fixes #6262
fixes #5439 — not quite a fix but we stopped supporting render throttling on react 17 

Separated rendering of shapes into a separate static canvas and rendering of UI-related things (remote cursors, selections, bindings, highlights and etc.) into an interactive canvas. This introduces the separation of concerns between the two canvases and significantly improves large-scene performance and UX when there is no need to re-render all the already drawn elements below.

_What is now part of the interactive canvas?_

![image](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/assets/20387666/078183be-ad8b-448b-94f1-949b60d8f988)

_How has the render flow changed?_

> Both `StaticCanvas` and `InteractiveCanvas` components are rendered conditionally with `React.memo()` based on the passed props.

> Currently, it is also essential that the `StaticCanvas` is rendered first due to the shape cache.

![image](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/assets/20387666/c487b956-d994-4172-90be-9e1e04185a55)

_How does this improve performance and UX?_

> I am limited to 144 Hz, meaning the maximum FPS on some examples below is potentially even higher.

https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/assets/20387666/71eb545b-b393-42fe-b041-eb1e68cc2c4d

https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/assets/20387666/0ec15015-9aed-4d76-bd28-52f22028aaed

https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/assets/20387666/0678f220-9aaf-4974-b715-5f8e18940272

_What could be improved even further?_

* `AppState` and handlers could be pushed down to the individual canvas components
* Optimising rendering of both canvases even more, i.e.:
  * `InteractiveCanvas` does not have to be rendered each time there is a scene mutation
  * It might not make sense to check against some app state properties, or it might make sense to check them deeply
* Some `AppState` props should not be shared in both canvases (i.e. `editingGroupId`, `selectedElementIds`, `frameToHighlight`)
* Other vertical partitioning strategies could be implemented, i.e.:
  * Dynamic canvas for the active element
  * Separate Multiplayer canvas for the collaborator object
  * Z-index based for the selected elements as discussed in #780
* Analysis of how `OffscreenCanvas` & workers could offload the calculation of the main thread, mainly for the `StaticCanvas` component
* Caching for some other critical functions, some of them are mentioned in the TODOs (i.e. frames & `isElementInFrame` & `getEligibleElementsForBinding`)
* Both canvases could be tested independently of each other, improving the performance of heavy tests and providing better separation of concerns
* Splitting whole `renderScene.ts` into independent renderers/modules 
* Scene being able to handle & cache `visibleElements` and canvas `elements`, so there would not be a need for `CanvasesWrapper`
* Both `canvas` and `interactiveCanvas` could have its own wrapper type so that they couldn't be interchanged

There's a race condition (due to canvases now being separate and each having its own rAF throttling) where the `shapeCache`'s shape is `null` in some calls of `renderInteractiveScene()` when rendering linear element point handles (midpoints), which causes the flickering and likely relates to the failing test as well.

![excal-bug-midpoints-flicker](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/assets/5153846/a2d9ac61-ba3d-4ada-b1bd-93825ae496bc)

Long term we need to either 1) make `ShapeCache` getter recalculate the shape if currently null, or 2) memoize on `version` (or whatever other key). Trouble is it'll either make perf worse in the latter (as we don't always have to recalculate on version change) or introduce other race conditions in the former (the cache could renew before the latest update is added to the elements array) and require rewrites (the shape cache needs to be moved to `Scene` class so it has access to latest elements).

Any idea for a quick solution in the meantime apart from disabling rAF throttling?

/cc @ad1992

> Any idea for a quick solution in the meantime apart from disabling rAF throttling?

I'm looking into tying the `shapeCache` to the `Renderer` class. Will require some refactor. But made me realize the way we're handling `rc` and `canvas` isn't safe (especially the way it's done this PR) where there are conditions in which the `rc` isn't defined yet even though we tell TS it is, so the rewrite will be for the best.

tests passing, flickering should be gone as well. The rewrites I made were specifically tailored to fix these issue, but they'll be a basis for further rewrites down the line to start decoupling renderer from the editor, and make it easier to use programmatically / on server.

That said, we need to re-test whether these changes didn't break anything as they are potentially significant.

Thanks! issue_context.title: split canvas rendering
issue_context.body:
For performance reasons, we should have at least 2 `<canvas>` elements:

1. one for elements (shapes) themselves. Sitting below.
2. one for UI things, such as selection/bounding boxes, remote client cursors, etc. Sitting above.

UI-related things change more often than elements, which affects performance in hot paths such as displaying remote client cursors on movement.
comments: a beginner question: why do we need canvas when using svg elements?

@7flash for export, not necessarily, but we'll need to properly decouple the SVG renderer from the canvas. For editing purposes, Excalidraw currently doesn't support SVG-only renderer, although it's also a possibility to add in the future.
